PHI (φ) is the golden ratio (1.618). The brand name is intentionally the mathematical symbol — it represents precision, proportion, and the Fibonacci system that underpins all spacing decisions.
Critical: The φ symbol is NOT decorative; it is conceptual and must be respected in all communications. It connects the brand name directly to the mathematical principle of perfect proportion.
The PHI Fiduciaire palette is built around deep teal, drawing on Swiss precision and Geneva's lakeside environment. Every color has a defined, limited role.

PHI Fiduciaire uses two typefaces: one editorial serif for display, one clean sans for body text. The contrast between these families IS the design — never substitute or mix additional typefaces.

All spacing is derived from the Fibonacci sequence, starting at 13px. This creates a mathematically harmonious rhythm that mirrors the φ symbol itself.
All repeating bands use Fibonacci values: 34px and 55px alternating. This creates a palindrome rhythm that draws the eye to the center naturally.
Palindrome rhythm: 34 / 55 / [photo] / 55 / 34 — the eye is drawn to the center naturally. Never break this proportional system.
These seven principles govern all visual decisions for PHI Fiduciaire. They are non-negotiable rules, not guidelines.
Each section must have a distinct visual treatment. Ghost numbers in Services → red accent lines in Why PHI → duotone images in Blog → etc. Repetition dilutes impact.
Never crowd content. When in doubt, add more breathing room. Whitespace communicates luxury and confidence.
Every alignment is intentional. Left-aligned text blocks, controlled grid systems, nothing arbitrary. If something cannot be justified, it does not belong.
Red is a Signal, Not Decoration
Use the red accent maximum 2–3 times per viewport. It should feel like punctuation, not color. When red appears everywhere, it means nothing.
Fewer elements, more space, higher quality. Avoid adding decorative elements that do not serve meaning. Subtract before you add.
On dark sections, a giant semi-transparent "φ" character (Cormorant Garamond, ~500px, 2–3% opacity) can appear as a background texture. Used in Final CTA only. Never overdone.
Combine a large Cormorant Garamond display line with a much smaller DM Sans body — the contrast IS the design. Scale difference should be dramatic, not subtle.
